extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, editorial_board_members, publishers, and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: An index of COPE guidance documents covering best practices and ethical standards for scholarly publishing, including journal management, peer review, retractions, authorship disputes, and handling of potential misconduct. The page lists individual guideline titles with short summaries and links to full guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for managing the relationships between society-owned journals, their society, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of ‘Learned Societies’ and ‘Professional Associations’ are an important part of the scientific literature. Regardless of the publication arrangements (i.e., self-published by the society, published under contract with a professional publishing house, or some combination of both) and the number of journals affiliated with that society, the policies of and the relationships among the…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance aimed at clarifying policies and relationships between societies, their journals, and publishers to ensure ethical and high-quality management of society-owned journals. (Page provides web and PDF versions; full recommendations are available in the linked guidance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), the Open Access Scholarly Publishers Association (OASPA), and the World Association of Medical Editors (WAME) are scholarly o…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint principles setting out transparency and best-practice standards for scholarly publishers; page notes Version 3 (January 2018) and a poster version (January 2018). Full principles available in the linked document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals’ Best Practices for ensuring consent for publishing medical case reports: guidance from COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication of case reports is a common practice in medical journals, and increasingly in basic science journals when an article illustrates a specific scientific point (e.g., a genetic phenotype). There is no doubt that case reports are valuable in the academic literature. However, they pose a specific ethical challenge for journals because, by their ve…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance focuses on ensuring appropriate consent for publication of medical case reports (and similar identifiable clinical material), outlining best practices around obtaining and documenting consent and dealing with privacy/ethical concerns. Full guidance available via the linked page/PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of Information Among Editors-in-Chief Regarding Possible Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: …Sharing of Information Among Editors-in-Chief Regarding Possible Misconduct. This guidance has been drafted following a COPE Discussion Forum (4 September 2013) and
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers when and how editors-in-chief can and should share information about suspected or confirmed misconduct, including considerations around complaints and appeals, conflicts of interest/competing interests, and ethical oversight. (See linked guidance for procedures and examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Editors: research, audit and service evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations regarding what type of study requires ethical approval vary worldwide. In some countries all studies require ethical approval but in others not. This may lead to submission to journals of manuscripts relating to such studies that do not satisfy the journal’s normal requirement for independent ethical approval, and rejection of the manuscript because of misunderstanding of local regu…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for editors on distinguishing research from audit or service evaluations and on assessing whether submitted work required independent ethical approval; helps editors avoid inappropriate rejections due to differing national regulations. Full guidance in linked document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases: guidance COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary. Institutions and journals both have important duties relating to research and publication misconduct. Institutions are responsible for the conduct of their researchers and for encouraging a healthy research environment. Journals are responsible for the conduct of their editors, for safeguarding the research record, and for ensuring the reliability of everything t…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out roles and responsibilities of institutions and journals when handling research integrity cases, advising on cooperation, information sharing, investigation triggers, and protection of the research record. See full guidance for procedural recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of Learned Societies are an important part of the scientific literature. Their management should be of the highest quality and ethically sound. First, the relationship of Editors of the journals of Learned Societies to those Societies is often complex. However, notwithstanding the economic and political realities of their journals, directors of Learned Societies should respe…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations for boards/directors of learned society journals on ethical governance, respecting editorial independence, and ensuring high-quality journal management. Full guidance available in linked web/PDF version.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle authorship disputes: a guide for new researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the main tasks of COPE’s education committee is to reduce unethical behaviour. This involves the rather bold step of defining when people have been behaving unethically, and then providing suggestions on how they can avoid doing so in the future. To this end we have written, and tested on a group of authors, a guide for young researchers on the area of authorship, which many people agree…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at new researchers: explains what constitutes unethical authorship practices, how disputes arise, and practical steps to prevent and resolve authorship disputes. (Linked guide and PDF provide examples and suggested processes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in all its forms plays an important role in ensuring the integrity of the scholarly record. The process depends to a large extent on trust, and requires that everyone involved behaves responsibly and ethically. Peer reviewers play a central and critical part in the peer-review process, but too often come to the role without any guidance and unaware of their ethical obligations. COPE…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out ethical obligations and expected behaviours for peer reviewers (confidentiality, conflicts of interest, timeliness, objectivity, constructive feedback), intended to guide reviewers who may lack prior training. Full checklist and examples are available in the linked guidance/PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text recycling guidelines for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A common issue encountered by editors is overlap of text with an author’s own previously published work, particularly with the increasing use of plagiarism detection software. This practice is known as ‘text recycling’ (also sometimes referred to as ‘self-plagiarism’). Opinions on the acceptability of text recycling vary greatly and it can be a challenge for editors to know how to deal with it…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for editors on identifying and handling text recycling/self-plagiarism, including how to interpret similarity reports, when recycling may be acceptable (e.g., methods), and when action should be taken. See linked document for examples and recommended policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary. COPE's Retraction guidelines for advice and guidance for editors. Journal editors should consider retracting a publication if: they have clear evidence that the findings are unreliable, either as a result of misconduct (e.g. data fabrication) or falsification (eg image…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides criteria for retraction and guidance on retraction notices and processes — e.g., retract when findings are unreliable due to misconduct or error, with further procedural advice on post-publication discussions and corrections. Full guidance available via link/PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: A short guide to ethical editing for new editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Background/structure. Becoming an editor of a journal is an exciting but daunting task, especially if you are working alone without day to day contact with editorial colleagues. This short guide aims to summarise key issues and to provide links to relevant pages of the COPE website as well as those of other organisations. 1. Initial assessment of journal wh…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical short-form guidance for new editors covering initial assessment of submissions/journal practices, key ethical issues, and links to more detailed COPE resources. Intended as an introductory checklist and primer; full content on linked page/PDF.
